extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (mathematicians and programmers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation of PARI/GP library and GP language functions: their semantics, allowed types, special cases, and library syntax. Useful for programming with PARI/GP and understanding type/precision behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: conj(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate of x. For real quadratic numbers, conjugation is in the real quadratic field. No effect on integers, reals, integermods, fractions or p-adics. polmod is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gconj(x). See conjvec for polmod conjugates.

rubrics_metrics.name: conjvec(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate vector representation of x. For polmod x = Mod(a,q), returns vector of length degree(q) with complex embeddings if q has integral/rational coefficients, otherwise conjugates if q has integermod coefficients. If x is integer or rational returns x. If x is a vector, returns matrix whose columns are conjugate vectors of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: conjvec(x, prec). Order matches polroots.

rubrics_metrics.name: denominator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowest denominator of x. For rationals or rational functions it is the usual denominator. For integers or polynomials returns 1. For vectors/matrices returns lowest common denominator of components. Other types forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: floor(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floor of x: for real x, the largest integer ≤ x. For rational functions, returns the Euclidean quotient of numerator by denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: frac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fractional part of x, defined as x − floor(x). For real x result in [0,1[.

rubrics_metrics.name: imag(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginary part of x. For quadratic numbers, it is the coefficient of ω in the canonical integral basis (1, ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: length(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of non-code words in x really used (effective length minus 2 for integers and polynomials). Degree of polynomial = length − 1. For t_STR returns number of letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: glength(x). Returns a C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifts an element x = a mod n of Z/nZ to a in Z; similarly lifts a polmod to a polynomial if v omitted. If v given, lifts only polmods with main variable v (if v not in x, lifts only intmods). For fractions, complex, quadratic, polynomial, power series, rational function, vector, matrix, lift is done on coefficients. Forbidden types: reals and p-adics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: lift0(x, v) where v is a long; omitted v coded as −1. Also lift(x) = lift0(x,-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: norm(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic norm: product of x with its conjugate (no square roots), or product of conjugates for polmods. For vectors/matrices taken componentwise (not L2-norm). Norm of R element is its square to be compatible with complex norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: norml2(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of the L2-norm of x. x must be a row or column vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator of x. For rationals/rational functions gives numerator. For integer or polynomial returns x itself. For vector/matrix numerator(x) = denominator(x)*x. Other types forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: numtoperm(n,k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates the k-th permutation (row vector length n) of numbers 1..n. k taken modulo n!; inverse of permtonum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: permute(n, k) where n is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: padicprec(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute p-adic precision of object x: minimum precision of components. Returns VERYBIGINT if x is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: padicprec(x, p). Result is a long integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: permtonum(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a permutation x on n elements, returns k such that x = numtoperm(n,k). Inverse of numtoperm.

rubrics_metrics.name: precision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives precision in decimal digits of PARI object x. If x exact returns largest single precision integer. If n provided creates new object equal to x with new precision n: for exact types no change; for vectors/matrices done componentwise; for real x n is number of significant decimal digits (truncates or extends with zeros); for p-adic or power series n is desired number of significant p-adic or X-adic digits. Function never changes the type of result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: precision0(x, n) where n is a long. Also ggprecision(x) (result GEN) and gprec(x, n). Use truncate to change type (e.g. power series → polynomial).

rubrics_metrics.name: random({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives random integer between 0 and N−1. Internal PARI RNG (linear congruences) not well distributed in arithmetic progressions. N can be arbitrarily large.

rubrics_metrics.name: real(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real part of x. For quadratic numbers, the coefficient of 1 in canonical integral basis (1, ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: round(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Rounds real x to nearest integer and sets e to number of error bits (binary exponent of difference between original and rounded value). If exponent of x too large compared to precision (e>0), result undefined and error if e not given. Operates on every coefficient at every level of PARI object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: grndtoi(x, &e) where e is a long integer. Also available: ground(x). Useful to get exact results after long approximate computations when theory predicts integer coefficients. Examples show behavior on power series.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tries to simplify object x by changing types when possible: converts complex/quadratic numbers with zero imaginary part to real, polynomials of degree zero to constant term, and recurses. Useful before arithmetic functions expecting integer arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: simplify(x). Note: does not concern rational function simplifications (PARI does that automatically).

rubrics_metrics.name: sizebyte(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs total number of bytes occupied by the tree representing PARI object x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: taille2(x) which returns a long. Function taille returns number of words instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: sizedigit(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs a quick bound for number of decimal digits of components of x (off by at most 1). For exact value use length(Str(x)) but slower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gsize(x) which returns a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Truncates x and sets e to number of error bits. For real x, chops fractional part; e is binary exponent of difference. If exponent too large relative to precision and e not given, error. Applies componentwise for rational functions and vectors/matrices; e is maximal number of error bits. Special uses: applied to power series transforms into polynomial or rational function by chopping O(X^k); applied to p-adics transforms into integer or rational by chopping O(p^k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gcvtoi(x, &e) where e is long. Also available: gtrunc(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: valuation(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes highest exponent of p dividing x. If p integer, x must be integer, integermod (with modulus divisible by p), fraction, q-adic with q=p, polynomial or power series (valuation = min valuation of coefficients). If p polynomial, x must be polynomial or rational function (and power series if x is a monomial). Valuation of vector, complex or quadratic number is minimum of component valuations. If x=0, result is VERYBIGINT for exact objects; for p-adics/power series result is exponent of zero. Other type combinations give error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ggval(x, p). Result is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: variable(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives main variable of object x, and p if x is p-adic. Error if x has no variable. Useful in GP; in library mode use gvar or test t_PADIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gpolvar(x). In library mode avoid gpolvar; test whether x is p-adic (type t_PADIC) and get p from x[2], or call gvar(x) which returns variable number/BIGINT otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental functions: general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: General behavior of transcendental functions depending on argument types: exact integer/real/rational/complex/quadratic are first converted to real/complex using default realprecision; in library mode supply prec parameter for exact types; precision argument semantics differ between GP and library mode. For integermod and p-adic only some functions implemented. For polynomial/power series/rational functions, they are converted to power series using precdl and Taylor expansion around X=0. For vectors/matrices evaluation is componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes about precision semantics (prec word-count in library mode vs decimal digits in GP), machine-word parity issues (32 vs 64 bit), principal branches chosen for multi-valued functions, and special remarks on p-adic/integral-mod behaviors and series expansion using global precdl in library mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: ^(power) operator
rubrics_metrics.description: If y not integer, x^y computed as exp(y*ln(x)). Can be applied to p-adic numbers as well as usual types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's constant γ ≈ 0.57721...; reserved name (cannot be used as variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mpeuler(prec) where prec must be given. Creates γ on PARI stack and a copy on heap for faster reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: I
rubrics_metrics.description: The complex unit √−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: global variable gi (type GEN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pi
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mppi(prec) where prec must be given. Creates π on PARI stack and a heap copy for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: abs(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute value (or modulus for complex). Power series and rational functions not allowed. Unlike other transcendental functions, exact argument not converted to real; returns exact result if possible. For polynomial returns −x if leading coefficient real and negative else x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gabs(x, prec). Examples shown for integers and complex rationals and reals.

rubrics_metrics.name: acos(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arccos: Re(acos(x)) ∈ [0, π]. If |x|>1 then result complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: acosh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arccosh: Im(acosh(x)) ∈ [0, π]. If x real and x<1 result complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gach(x, prec). Principal square root chosen for complex/negative numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: agm(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic-geometric mean of x and y. p-adic or power series arguments allowed; p-adic agm exists only if x/y ≡ 1 (mod p) (mod 16 for p=2). x and y cannot both be vectors or matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: arg(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument of complex number x with −π < arg(x) ≤ π.

rubrics_metrics.name: asin(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arcsin: Re(asin(x)) ∈ [−π/2, π/2]. If real and |x|>1 result complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: asinh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arsinh: Im(asinh(x)) ∈ [−π/2, π/2].

rubrics_metrics.name: atan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arctan: Re(atan(x)) ∈ (−π/2, π/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: atanh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of arctanh: Im(atanh(x)) ∈ (−π/2, π/2]. If real and |x|>1 result complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernfrac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli number B_x as rational number. Argument x should be integer (B0=1, B1=−1/2, B2=1/6...).

rubrics_metrics.name: bernreal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli number B_x returned as a real with current precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernvec(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates vector of Bernoulli numbers [B0, B2, ..., B2x] as rationals. Example provided to define bern(k) using bernvec for efficiency when many values needed; calling bernfrac(k) is more efficient if few values needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: besseljh(n, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: J-Bessel function of half-integral index: computes J_{n+1/2}(x) where n integer and x any complex. Not very accurate for small x in this version.

rubrics_metrics.name: besselk(nu, x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: K-Bessel function of index nu (can be complex) and argument x. Present implementation accepts only real positive x. If flag=1 uses alternative implementation often faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: kbessel(nu, x, prec) and kbessel2(nu, x, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cos(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosine function.

rubrics_metrics.name: cosh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic cosine.

rubrics_metrics.name: cotan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotangent function.

rubrics_metrics.name: dilog(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of the dilogarithm (analytic continuation of ∑_{n≥1} x^n/n^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: eint1(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential integral ∫_x^∞ e^{−t}/t dt for x ∈ R. If n present outputs n-dimensional vector [eint1(x), ..., eint1(n x)] which is faster than repeated calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: veceint1(x, n, prec). Also eint1(x, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: erfc(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementary error function (2/√π) ∫_x^∞ e^{−t^2} dt.

rubrics_metrics.name: eta(x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedekind's η function without q^{1/24}. If x complex with Im(x)>0 returns ∏_{n≥1}(1−q^n) where q=e^{2π i x}. If x power series with positive valuation returns ∏_{n≥1}(1−x^n). If flag=1 and x convertible to complex computes true η including q^{1/24}.

rubrics_metrics.name: exp(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential function. p-adic arguments with positive valuation accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: gammah(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gamma function evaluated at x + 1/2; faster when x integer than using gamma(x+1/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: gamma(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gamma function. p-adic gamma not implemented in this version.

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperu(a, b, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: U-confluent hypergeometric function with parameters a and b (can be complex) and argument x. Implementation requires x positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: hyperu(a, b, x, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: incgam(s, x, {y})
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete gamma function ∫_x^∞ e^{−t} t^{s−1} dt with x positive and s real. If y given (assumed Γ(s)) it speeds computation for small x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: incgam(s, x, prec) and incgam4(s, x, y, prec). Internal helper functions incgam1/incgam2 exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: incgamc(s, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementary incomplete gamma function ∫_0^x e^{−t} t^{s−1} dt. Arguments s and x must be positive; behavior differs when x too large.

rubrics_metrics.name: log(x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of natural logarithm with Im(ln(x)) ∈ (−π, π]. For real x<0 the result is complex with imaginary part π. p-adic arguments accepted with convention ln(p)=0 (so exp(ln(x))/x may differ by root of unity/power of p). If flag=1 use agm formula suggested by Mestre when x real; otherwise identical to log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: glog(x, prec) or glogagm(x, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lngamma(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of logarithm of Gamma function. Can accept much larger arguments than gamma. p-adic version not implemented in this version.

rubrics_metrics.name: polylog(m, x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Various polylogarithms depending on flag: flag=0 m-th polylogarithm (analytic continuation of ∑ x^n/n^m) using power series when |x|^2 ≤ 1/2 else expansion in log(x); valid in large domain but avoid far from unit circle. Flags 1–3 give modified polylogarithms (variants of Zagier's D̃_m, D_m, P_m) with detailed series expansions involving logs and limits. These satisfy functional equation f_m(1/x) = (−1)^{m−1} f_m(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: polylog0(m, x, flag, prec). Power series, polynomial, rational and vector/matrix arguments allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: psi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: ψ-function (digamma): logarithmic derivative Γ'(x)/Γ(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sin(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sine function.

rubrics_metrics.name: sinh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic sine.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqr(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of x. Not always identical to x*x because squaring can be implemented more efficiently and can increase p-adic precision (e.g., 2-adic). Function also used when multiplying two identical objects to exploit efficiency. Examples show different p-adic precision behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrt(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of square root with Arg(sqrt(x)) ∈ (−π/2, π/2] and chosen so that (Re(sqrt(x))>0) or (Re=0 and Im≥0). For real x<0 result complex with positive imaginary part. Integermod with prime modulus and p-adics allowed: returns square root whose first p-adic digit lies in [0,p/2]. For integermod non-prime or non-prime-adic behavior undefined.

rubrics_metrics.name: tan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangent function.

rubrics_metrics.name: tanh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic tangent.

rubrics_metrics.name: teichmuller(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teichmüller character of the p-adic number x.

rubrics_metrics.name: theta(q, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jacobi theta-function θ(q,z).

rubrics_metrics.name: thetanullk(q, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: k-th derivative at z=0 of theta(q,z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: thetanullk(q, k, prec) where k is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: weber(x, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Weber's three f functions. flag=0 returns f(x)=exp(−iπ/24)·η((x+1)/2)/η(x) with relation to j-invariant; flag=1 returns f1(x)=η(x/2)/η(x); flag=2 returns sqrt(2)η(2x)/η(x). Various identities and relations between f,f1,f2 and j provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: weber0(x, flag, prec), or wf(x, prec), wf1(x, prec), wf2(x, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: zeta(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Riemann zeta function ζ(s)=∑_{n≥1} n^{−s}. Computed using Euler-Maclaurin summation except when s integer: uses Bernoulli numbers for s≤0 or s>0 even, and modular forms for s>0 odd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic functions: overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic functions (natural domain Z or Z>0, sometimes polynomials) accept only integer and polynomial types (vector/matrix applied componentwise). In current version, arithmetic functions (e.g., totient, Möbius, divisor sums) call factoring machinery after trial division and rely on probabilistic primality tests; includes Pollard Rho, ECM, MPQS, with early exit options for moebius and issquarefree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: factorint engine uses probabilistic primality testing (Rabin-Miller) so primality declarations may be probabilistic. This paragraph outlines algorithmic dependencies for arithmetic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qfb(a,b,c,{D=0.})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates binary quadratic form ax^2 + bxy + cy^2. If b^2 − 4ac > 0 initialize Shanks' distance function to D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: Qfb0(a,b,c,D,prec). Also qfi(a,b,c) when b^2−4ac<0, and qfr(a,b,c,d) when b^2−4ac>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: addprimes({x=[]})
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds primes in vector x (or integer x) to user-specified extra primes table (appended to table computed on GP init). Returns 100-component row vector: first entries contain primes added, last entries filled with 1's. If x empty returns current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries not checked for primality; can add composite numbers. Present PARI allows up to 100 user-specified primes; limit controlled by NUMPRTBELT in init.c. Use removeprimes to delete entries. Arithmetic functions like eulerphi do not use this extra table. Library syntax: addprimes(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestappr(x, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: For real x, finds best rational approximation to x with denominator ≤ k using continued fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: bezout(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds u and v minimal in natural sense such that x*u + y*v = gcd(x,y). Arguments both integers or both polynomials. Result is row vector [u, v, gcd].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: vecbezout(x, y) to get vector, or gbezout(x, y, &u, &v) returns address of gcd and fills u,v with addresses of created objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: bezoutres(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: As bezout but resultant of x and y replaces gcd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: vecbezoutres(x, y) or subresext(x, y, &u, &v) which returns address of created gcd and fills u,v.

rubrics_metrics.name: bigomega(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of prime divisors of |x| counted with multiplicity. x must be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: bigomega(x). Returns a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: binomial(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binomial coefficient (x choose y). y must be integer, x can be any PARI object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: binome(x, y) where y is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinese(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chinese remainder: given x and y returns z in same residue classes as x and y when possible. If x and y both integermods or polmods, creates with same modulus type. Operation applies recursively to vector/matrix arguments (componentwise) and per-coefficient for polynomials. chinese(x,x)=x always.

rubrics_metrics.name: content(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes gcd of all coefficients of x where meaningful. If scalar returns x. If polynomial or power series returns usual content. If rational function returns ratio of contents of numerator and denominator. If vector/matrix returns gcd of all entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: contfrac(x, {b}, {lmax})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates row vector of partial quotients of continued fraction expansion of x, limited to lmax partial quotients. For real x stops at last significant partial quotient if lmax omitted. x can be rational function or power series. If vector b supplied numerators equal to coefficients of b and length equals length(b) unless partial remainder equals zero, in which case expansion stops; stopping criterion differs for reals when b too long (some partial quotients may be insignificant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: contfrac0(x, b, lmax). Also available gboundcf(x, lmax), gcf(x), gcf2(b,x) where lmax is C integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: contfracpnqn(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x vector or one-row matrix [a0,...,an] considers it as continued fraction partial quotients and returns 2x2 matrix [pn, pn−1; qn, qn−1] with pn/qn = continued fraction value. If x matrix with two rows [b0,..bn] and [a0,..an], treat as generalized continued fraction pn/qn = 1/b0(a0 + b1/(a1 + ...)).

rubrics_metrics.name: core(n, {flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: If non-zero integer n = d f^2 with d squarefree returns d. If flag non-zero returns [d, f].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: core0(n, flag). Also core(n)=core(n,0) and core2(n)=core(n,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: coredisc(n, {flag})
rubrics_metrics.description: If non-zero integer n = d f^2 with d fundamental discriminant (incl. 1) returns d. If flag non-zero returns [d,f]. Note: if n not ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4, f may be half-integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: coredisc0(n, flag). Also coredisc(n)=coredisc(n,0) and coredisc2(n)=coredisc(n,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: dirdiv(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x and y are vectors considered as Dirichlet series (perhaps different lengths but y[1]≠0), computes quotient x/y as vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: direuler(p = a, b, expr, {c})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes Dirichlet series to b terms of Euler product of expr as p ranges primes from a to b. expr must be polynomial or rational function in variable other than p (say X) and expr(X) understood as local factor expr(p^{−s}). If c present output only first c coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: direuler(entree *ep, GEN a, GEN b, char *expr). See sums/products section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirmul(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x,y vectors considered as Dirichlet series (possibly differing lengths) compute product x*y as vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: divisors(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates row vector of positive divisors of integer x in increasing order. Factorization from factor can be used instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: eulerphi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's totient φ(|x|) = |(Z/xZ)^*|. x must be integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor(x, {lim = −1})
rubrics_metrics.description: General factorization. For integer, rational, polynomial or rational function returns two-column matrix: irreducible factors and exponents. For vector/matrix factor componentwise. By definition 0 factored as 0^1. For integer/rational optional lim argument restricts search for factors up to lim (or primelimit), possibly leaving composite remainder. Polynomials/rational functions must have scalar coefficients; PARI factors polynomials up to multiplication by constant and discards content. PARI attempts to guess factoring ring sensibly. Multivariate factoring not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: factor0(x, lim) where lim is a C integer. Also factor(x)=factor0(x,−1), smallfact(x)=factor0(x,0). See factornf for number field factoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback(f, {nf})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any factorization f, reconstructs the factored object. If nf supplied, f assumed prime ideal factorization in number field nf and resulting ideal given in HNF form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: factorback(f, nf) where omitted nf entered as NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using distinct degree plus Cantor–Zassenhaus. Coefficients of x must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Result two-column matrix of irreducible factors and exponents. For only degrees use factormod(x,p,1). factormod usually faster than factorcantor.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff(x, p, a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x in finite field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p. Coefficients of x must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Result two-column matrix of irreducible factors and exponents. Recommended to use distinct variable name for a to keep lift() of result legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial(x) or x!
rubrics_metrics.description: Factorial operation. Expression x! returns integer result, while factorial(x) returns a real number. x must be a long integer and not a PARI integer for certain library routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mpfact(x) for x! and mpfactr(x, prec) for factorial(x). x must be C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors integer n using combination of Pollard Rho (Brent), Lenstra ECM (Montgomery), and MPQS (adapted from LiDIA), and search for pure powers with exponent ≤10. Output two-column matrix as for factor. flag optional with binary digits meaning: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first stage ECM, 4 avoid Rho, 8 don't run final ECM (may declare huge composite as prime). Probabilistic primality testing used; composites might (very rarely) not be detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factorint gives direct access to integer factoring engine used by arithmetic functions. Engine is somewhat experimental but faster on average than pure ECM at expense of memory. Users invited to experiment with flag settings and GP's debuglevel to watch internals. Library syntax: factorint(n, flag).
